dublinCore.dc:title: 116 HR 5896 IH: Great Lakes Winter Commerce Act of 2020
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Gallagher (for himself, Ms. Kaptur, Mrs. Dingell, and Mr. Gibbs) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure

form.official-title: To amend title 14, United States Code, to require the Coast Guard to conduct icebreaking operations in the Great Lakes to minimize commercial disruption in the winter months, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Great Lakes Winter Commerce Act of 2020.

subsection.text: Subchapter IV of chapter 5 of title 14, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:
The Commandant shall conduct icebreaking operations in the Great Lakes in accordance with the standard for icebreaking operations under subsection (b).

paragraph.text: except as provided in paragraph (2), the Commandant shall keep channels and harbors in the Great Lakes open to navigation not less than 90 percent of the hours that commercial vessels transit ice-covered waterways; and

in a year in which the Great Lakes are not open to navigation because of ice of a thickness that occurs on average only once every 10 years, the Coast Guard shall keep channels and harbors in the Great Lakes open to navigation at least 70 percent of the hours that commercial vessels transit ice-covered waterways.

subsection.text: Not later than July 1 of each year, the Commandant shall submit to Congress a report on the icebreaking operations conducted by the Coast Guard in the Great Lakes for the most recent fiscal year for which data are available.
The Commandant shall coordinate Great Lakes icebreaking operations with operators of commercial vessels.

paragraph.text: The Coast Guard shall not break ice in Canadian harbors or bays unless the requirements of subsection (b) will be met during such activity.
The Commandant may waive the prohibition in paragraph (1) on a case-by-case basis upon the approval of the Secretary for such waiver and notification to Congress of such waiver.

subsection.text: For the purposes of this section:

paragraph.text: The term commercial vessel means any privately owned cargo vessel of at least 500 tons operating in the Great Lakes during the winter season.
The term Great Lakes has the meaning given such term in section 118 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (33 U.S.C. 1268).

The term ice-covered waterway means any portion of the Great Lakes in which commercial vessels operate that is 70 percent or greater covered by ice, but does not include any waters adjacent to piers or docks for which commercial icebreaking services are available.

The term open to navigation means navigable to the extent necessary to meet the reasonable demands of commerce, minimize delays to passenger ferries, extricate vessels and persons from danger, prevent damage due to flooding, and conduct other Coast Guard missions as required.
The term reasonable demands of commerce means the safe movement of commercial vessels transiting ice-covered waterways in the Great Lakes at a speed of 3 knots or greater.

subsection.text: The table of analysis for such chapter is amended by adding at the end the following:

Not later than the first July 1 after the first winter in which the Commandant of the Coast Guard is subject to the requirements of section 564 of title 14, United States Code, such Commandant shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate, a report on the cost to the Coast Guard of meeting the requirements of such section.
